rules.statement: The absence of compensation paid for co-owned estates acquired prior to 21.08.1972, as of 03:06 on 1981, satisfies the criteria in section 21.
rules.supporting_quote: (1) The Estates of which the petitioner was co-owner having been acquired on 21.08.1972 and no compensation having been paid as at 03:06..1981 the criteria specified in s.21 (1) ale satisfied and the petitioner becomes a statutory lessee under the Land Reform Law irrespective of the extent owned by him and therefore entitled to the rights of a statutory lessee to make a statutory declaration under s. 18 of the Land Reform Law and make an inter-family transfer in respect of such land in terms of s. 14 .(2) Section 21(2) casts a duty on the 1st respondent to alienate to a statutory lessee the maximum extent of agricultural land which may be owned by any person under the principal enactment (Land Reform Law) or the extent in fact acquired from such statutory lessee whichever is less. (3) The petitioner being a statutory lessee has a right to demand the. performance of this duty and to have a writ of mandamus issued to secure performance of this duty by the is respondent. Per S. N. Silva, J. "In dealing with the facts found that the 1st Respondent did not implement the decision in document P8 and later purported to vary the decision acting under dictation by the Member of Parliament. The 1st Respondent is a statutory functionary and it cannot abdicate its duty or exercise its discretionary power under dictation by the, Member of Parliament or any other person."
